title: Every Friday at Five

pre.en: Why was the Friday report cancelled?
pre.zh: 周五的报告为什么被取消了？
options: The client was angry about the delay.
Nobody on the team wanted to write it.
Rachel decided it took too much time.
Nobody at the client had read it for two years.

intro: 一个工作小故事：每周五准时发出的报告，有一个周五谁也没发。周一大家回忆各自说过什么、以为谁会做什么。读的时候留意间接引语：Rachel asked if …、Arjun told her …、I said … 把别人的话转述出来，时态往往往过去退一步；也看看组长 Rachel 出了问题是怎么处理的。

sentences.en: So, every Friday, our team sends a status report to the client.
sentences.zh: 是这样，每周五我们团队都要给客户发一份进度报告。

sentences.en: Arjun writes it, I check it, and Rachel approves it.
sentences.zh: Arjun 写，我检查，Rachel 审批。

sentences.en: Then at five o'clock, it goes out.
sentences.zh: 然后五点整发出去。

sentences.en: The team's done it like this for three years, so everyone knows what they're supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 团队这么干已经三年了，所以每个人都清楚自己该干什么。

sentences.en: Well, last Friday was crazy, and somehow the report slipped everyone's mind.
sentences.zh: 结果上周五忙疯了，不知怎么的，报告的事大家全忘了。

sentences.en: On Monday morning, Rachel asked if anyone had sent it.
sentences.zh: 周一上午，Rachel 问有没有人把报告发出去了。

sentences.en: Arjun told her he'd sent it to me at three.
sentences.zh: Arjun 说他三点就发给我了。

sentences.en: I said I'd checked it and passed it on to her.
sentences.zh: 我说我检查完了，已经转给她了。

sentences.en: And Rachel said she'd approved it at half past four.
sentences.zh: Rachel 说她四点半就批了。

sentences.en: It turned out we'd all thought someone else was going to send it.
sentences.zh: 原来，我们每个人都以为会有别人发。

sentences.en: So who was to blame?
sentences.zh: 那到底该怪谁？

sentences.en: I was sure I'd let the team down.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得，肯定是我拖了大家后腿。

sentences.en: I mean, we'd kept the client waiting all weekend!
sentences.zh: 要知道，我们让客户白等了一整个周末啊！

sentences.en: They must have been annoyed.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定很恼火。

sentences.en: And they might have got the wrong idea about our team.
sentences.zh: 说不定还对我们团队有了误会。

sentences.en: How could we possibly forget?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么会忘了呢？

sentences.en: I just wanted to send it as soon as possible, with a big apology.
sentences.zh: 我只想赶紧把报告发过去，再好好道个歉。

sentences.en: But Rachel didn't lose her temper.
sentences.zh: 可 Rachel 没发火。

sentences.en: She said it was her fault, not ours, and she took responsibility for the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 她说这是她的错，不怪我们，把责任全揽了下来。

sentences.en: She also pointed out that nobody was actually in charge of pressing Send.
sentences.zh: 她还指出，其实根本没有人负责按「发送」。

sentences.en: Then she said she'd follow up with the client herself, and picked up the phone.
sentences.zh: 然后她说她亲自去跟客户沟通，说完就拿起了电话。

sentences.en: Ten minutes later, she put the phone down with a strange grin.
sentences.zh: 十分钟后，她放下电话，脸上挂着一丝古怪的笑。

sentences.en: "Good news, Chen," she said.
sentences.zh: 「好消息，小陈，」她说。

sentences.en: "The client asked me which report I meant."
sentences.zh: 「客户问我说的是哪份报告。」

sentences.en: "Apparently, our reports go to an old email address that nobody checks."
sentences.zh: 「原来我们的报告一直发到一个没人看的旧邮箱。」

sentences.en: "They stopped reading them two years ago."
sentences.zh: 「他们两年前就不看了。」

sentences.en: The report was cancelled that afternoon.
sentences.zh: 当天下午，这份报告就取消了。

sentences.en: Arjun said it was the best news he'd heard all year.
sentences.zh: Arjun 说，这是他今年听到的最好的消息。

cards.note: status 是项目的「状态、进展」；开会时「同步一下进度」可以说 give a quick status update。
approve sth 是批准某事；approve of sb/sth 是「赞成、看得惯」，意思不一样。名词是 approval。
used to say what someone should do because of a rule, a plan or what others expect
cards.tip: 强调规定、安排或别人的期望，常暗示实际上没做到：I was supposed to call him.（本该打电话，结果没打）。
cards.example: I'm supposed to send the build to QA by six, but it's still failing.

cards.note: 说不清原因时用：Somehow I lost my keys. 也可以表示「想办法、总归」：We'll finish it somehow.
if something slips your mind, you forget it
cards.tip: 主语是被忘掉的事，不是人：It slipped my mind，不说 I slipped my mind。your 要换成对应的人：slipped his mind、slipped everyone's mind。
cards.example: Sorry, your email completely slipped my mind — I'll reply today.

cards.note: pass sth on to sb，代词放中间：pass it on。传话也能用：I'll pass on your message.
to happen in a way you did not expect, or to be discovered to be true
to be responsible for something bad that has happened
cards.tip: 形式是主动的，意思却是「该被怪」：Who is to blame?；怪的是什么事用 for：Nobody is to blame for the delay。
cards.example: The old router was to blame for the slow Wi-Fi.

cards.note: to not do what someone trusted or expected you to do
cards.tip: 代词放中间：let him down；let 的过去式和过去分词都是 let，没有 letted。
cards.example: I promised to help with the demo, and I don't want to let you down.

cards.note: to make someone wait, usually because you are late
cards.tip: 等的人放中间，后面用 waiting：keep sb waiting，不说 keep sb wait。迟到道歉常说 Sorry to keep you waiting。
cards.example: Sorry to keep you waiting — my last call ran over.

cards.note: to understand a situation wrongly
cards.tip: 误会谁或什么用 about：get the wrong idea about sb。英式英语的过去分词是 got，美式多用 gotten。
cards.example: Don't get the wrong idea — I'm not angry, just tired.

cards.note: as quickly as you can
to suddenly become very angry
It's my fault. 是「怪我」，强调责任在谁；mistake 只说「做错的事」。
to accept that something is your job or your fault
cards.tip: responsibility 前面不加 the；介词用 for，不用 of。比 be responsible for 更强调「主动认下来」。
cards.example: As team lead, I take responsibility for the delay.

cards.note: to tell someone something they did not know or had not noticed
cards.tip: 常接 that 从句：point out that …；指出某个东西，代词放中间：point it out。
cards.example: Thanks for pointing out the typo on the login screen.

cards.note: responsible for a person, group or piece of work
to contact someone again, or do more, after something has happened
cards.tip: 跟进某人用 with，跟进某事用 on：follow up with the client、follow up on the bug。名词写成 follow-up：a follow-up email。
cards.example: I'll follow up with an email after the meeting.

cards.note: client 多指买服务的客户，比如外包、咨询、律师的客户；在店里买东西的顾客是 customer。
to lift something, or to collect something that is waiting for you
转述刚听来的消息时常放句首，意思是「据说、听人说」；不是「显然」，「显然」是 obviously。
